name: Beard shaping guide
lead: A beard shaping guide is a plastic or metal template, often with preset curves for the cheek line and neckline, held against the face as an edge to trim or shave along. Some are sold as multi-piece kits. Its purpose is to give repeatable, symmetrical lines without relying on eyeballing in a mirror.

It has not been studied. The beard itself is an androgen-dependent secondary sexual characteristic, and Grokipedia summarises average growth of about 0.5 inch per month, which determines how long a mistaken line takes to grow out.[1] Effects of a shaping guide last until the next trim.

paras: Guides are typically flexible plastic or rigid metal, with curved cutouts for different neckline heights and cheek-line shapes. Some flexible templates are reported to be imprecise.

The user holds the template to the face and trims or shaves the hair outside its edge, so the line matches on both sides. The placement of the neckline affects the beard's overall look, and a line set too high or low cannot be corrected until regrowth.

Beard growth is driven by androgens, especially dihydrotestosterone, acting on follicles of the lower face from puberty.[1] Grokipedia gives an average growth rate of about 13 mm per month with seasonal variation.[1] Shaving or trimming does not change thickness or growth rate according to that source.[1]

Risk is limited to nicks and irritation when shaving the neck. The neck is a common site for pseudofolliculitis barbae, in which cut hairs re-enter the skin; a 2019 review recommends avoiding very close shaving, stretching the skin, and dry shaving.[2]
